AfterObtained.rationale: CLOSED 2026-07-28 (round 3) by the gap-queue continuation's post-section-A pass -- the turn-start split, the combat-over hook gate, Glass Eye's reward set, the out-of-combat potion action and the choose-a-card selector arm. This is a CODE change, not a re-reading of the old code. All three remaining guards (G3, G4, G5) are closed together, because the relic now builds a real reward SET. `GlassEye.AfterObtained` constructs five CardRewardGroups -- Common, Common, Uncommon, Uncommon, Rare -- populates every one of them, runs `rewards.apply_reward_modifiers` (Hook.ModifyRewards' two passes) and only then hands the set to `RunState.offer_rewards`, the new RewardsCmd.OfferCustom seam the driver installs. Each group draws through `rewards.create_reward_cards`, which fires TryModifyCardRewardOptions and its Late pass (G3), uses `reward_pool_card_ids` on the parity path (G4), and -- per G1/G2's revision on this pass -- correctly SKIPS the upgrade roll on both paths via `CardCreationFlags.NO_UPGRADE_ROLL`, matching `GlassEye.cs:29`'s `ForNonCombatWithUniformOdds` factory call. EXECUTED: test/test_glass_eye_reward_set.py.  The gap it replaced read: NARROWED 2026-07-27. Of the four divergences this rollup carried, G1 is CLOSED -- glass_eye.py:43-59 now takes the per-card `run.player_rng.rewards.next_float()` upgrade roll before the is_upgradable test, so the screens spend 15 NextItem + 15 NextFloat on PlayerRng.Rewards as CardFactory.CreateForReward does -- and G2 is closed on the parity path (see that guard for the legacy-branch residue). WHAT REMAINS: G3, the reward-option hooks CardFactory fires inside CreateForReward are still never dispatched -- glass_eye.py builds options with make_card and hands them straight to run.select_cards, bypassing rewards.create_reward_cards' two-pass modify_card_reward_options / _late dispatch; G4, the candidate pool is still `pool_card_ids()` (FilterForCombat) where a reward draws from `reward_pool_card_ids()`, so Feed and Not Yet can never be offered; and G5, the five screens are still populated and resolved one at a time.

guards.what: G1 (CLOSED, REVERSED FROM ITS OWN EARLIER FIX): whether Glass Eye's 15 created cards take an upgrade roll at all
guards.issue: REVISED on this re-audit pass (source changed since the entry's last edit): `GlassEye.cs:29` builds its options via `CardCreationOptions.ForNonCombatWithUniformOdds(...)`, and that factory method itself ORs `CardCreationFlags.NoUpgradeRoll` onto the result (`CardCreationOptions.cs:162`, confirmed by reading the game source directly on this pass) BEFORE `.WithFlags(NoRarityModification)` adds a second flag on top -- so the C# creation carries BOTH flags, and `CardFactory.CreateForReward`'s upgrade-roll call (and the `rng.NextFloat()` inside it) never fires for any of the 15 cards. This is the OPPOSITE of what this entry said before ('C# rolls, the sim doesn't, add a roll') -- that earlier fix was wrong, and the CURRENT sim code has already been corrected past it: `sts2_rl/relics/glass_eye.py` builds each `CardRewardGroup` with `flags=CardCreationFlags.NO_UPGRADE_ROLL` (glass_eye.py:76), and `CardRewardGroup.populate` -> `create_reward_cards` (rewards.py:397) reads `roll_for_upgrade = not (flags & NO_UPGRADE_ROLL)` and skips both the roll and its draw when set (rewards.py:342-348, 393-397). The sim's own docstring at glass_eye.py:18-26 names this exactly: 'R14 finding, corrected from an earlier round's "neither is set" reading, which was wrong: it looked only at the visible `.WithFlags(...)` call and missed the flag the factory method itself ORs in.' Net effect: 0 upgrade-roll draws on 15 created cards on BOTH sides, not 15 and not 30 -- this record's own prior text asserting a 15-or-30-draw target was itself the divergence from the source, now closed by the R14 fix. `TryModifyCardRewardOptions` (both passes) is UNAFFECTED -- `NoUpgradeRoll` and `NoModifyHooks` are independent flags and only `NoRarityModification`+`NoUpgradeRoll` are set here (G3 stands).

guards.what: G2 (CLOSED, SAME REVERSAL AS G1): whether Glass Eye's non-Rare options can ever arrive pre-upgraded
guards.issue: Same correction as G1, same source fact: `ForNonCombatWithUniformOdds` sets `NoUpgradeRoll` unconditionally, so NEITHER side ever upgrades a Glass Eye reward option -- the game's `act_index * UpgradedCardOddScaling` odds this entry previously invoked never come into play for THIS relic's cards, because `RollForUpgrade` is skipped entirely, not merely rolled with some probability. `sts2_rl/relics/glass_eye.py` no longer has a legacy/parity split for the upgrade roll at all (the whole per-card upgrade-roll block this entry described has been removed along with the rest of the old open-coded implementation); both the parity and legacy paths run through the same `CardRewardGroup.populate` -> `create_reward_cards`, and `NO_UPGRADE_ROLL` is set on the group regardless of `run.rng_set`. Verified by reading `rewards.py:397` and `glass_eye.py:76` directly on this pass; the two are the same flag check on both draw paths, so there is no residual legacy-branch gap left to track.

guards.what: G3 (LIVE): CardFactory fires `Hook.TryModifyCardRewardOptions` (BOTH phases) at the end of every CreateForReward; the sim's glass_eye never dispatches modify_card_reward_options
guards.rationale: CLOSED 2026-07-28 (round 3) by the gap-queue continuation's post-section-A pass -- the turn-start split, the combat-over hook gate, Glass Eye's reward set, the out-of-combat potion action and the choose-a-card selector arm. This is a CODE change, not a re-reading of the old code. Every screen now draws through `rewards.create_reward_cards`, whose tail is CardFactory.cs:104-107 -- `Hook.TryModifyCardRewardOptions` and its Late pass over the finished option list. EXECUTED: test/test_glass_eye_reward_set.py::test_g3_the_option_hooks_reach_every_screen, and `py audit/tools/relic_probes_b06.py glass-eye` (3), where all five cards Glass Eye grants a Glitter run now carry Glam. NoModifyHooks is not among the flags GlassEye.cs:29 sets, so both passes are correct here.  The gap it replaced read: MECHANISM: CardFactory.cs:104 runs `if (!options.Flags.HasFlag(CardCreationFlags.NoModifyHooks) && Hook.TryModifyCardRewardOptions(...))`, and Hook.TryModifyCardRewardOptions (Hook.cs:1445-1468) walks every listener's TryModifyCardRewardOptions and then every listener's TryModifyCardRewardOptionsLate. GlassEye sets only NoRarityModification, so the hooks DO run on its five screens. HISTORICAL (pre-rewrite): glass_eye.py used to build the options with make_card and hand them straight to run.select_cards, bypassing the reward-options dispatch. Today it routes through CardRewardGroup.populate/create_reward_cards (rewards.py:639-649, 313-...), which fires the TryModifyCardRewardOptions bracket for every group. REACHABILITY (LIVE, executed -- `py audit/tools/relic_probes_b06.py glass-eye`): with relic/glitter in the run (Ancient, granted by the ported Nonupeipe shrine, and its port DOES implement modify_card_reward_options), Glass Eye's five granted cards come out as [breakthrough None, breakthrough None, pillage None, evil_eye None, barricade None) -- not one Glam, where the game Glams every eligible option. The same silence applies to the three egg relics (an offered Power would arrive un-upgraded with Frozen Egg in the run), to Silver Crucible, Silken Tress and Fresnel Lens. Note the fix is one call, but it must run BEFORE the options are shown, not after the pick.

guards.what: G4 (LIVE): the candidate pool is `pool_card_ids()` (FilterForCombat) where a reward draws from `GetUnlockedCards`, so Feed and Not Yet can never be offered
guards.rationale: CLOSED 2026-07-28 (round 3) by the gap-queue continuation's post-section-A pass -- the turn-start split, the combat-over hook gate, Glass Eye's reward set, the out-of-combat potion action and the choose-a-card selector arm. This is a CODE change, not a re-reading of the old code. The candidates come from `reward_pool_card_ids` on the parity path -- CardPool.GetUnlockedCards, which is what `options.GetPossibleCards(player)` resolves to -- so Feed and Not Yet really are offerable on the Rare screen. The Uniform branch is also now modelled properly: CardFactory.cs:219-221 takes NO rarity roll when RarityOdds == Uniform (the predicate narrows the pool and NextItem picks out of it), where the sim ran RollWithBaseOdds and burned one extra PlayerRng.Rewards draw per card. That fix is shared with Room Full of Cheese and The Future of Potions, the other two Uniform callers. EXECUTED: test/test_glass_eye_reward_set.py (g4 + the two uniform-branch tests) and `py audit/tools/relic_probes_b06.py glass-eye` (4).  The gap it replaced read: MECHANISM: GlassEye.cs:29 builds `CardCreationOptions.ForNonCombatWithUniformOdds(new [Owner.Character.CardPool], c => c.Rarity == rarity)`, and CreateForReward resolves the candidates through `options.GetPossibleCards(player)` minus the blacklist, then (Uniform branch) excludes only Basic and Ancient rarity (CardFactory.cs:216-225) -- the combat-only filter never applies to rewards. glass_eye.py:22, 24 imports and calls `pool_card_ids()`, whose docstring says it mirrors FilterForCombat and drops `can_be_generated_in_combat=False` cards (cards/pool.py:100-117). The sim HAS the right helper: `reward_pool_card_ids()` (cards/pool.py:120-133) exists for exactly this and its docstring names Feed and NotYet as the affected cards. REACHABILITY (LIVE, executed -- `py audit/tools/relic_probes_b06.py glass-eye`): the reward-eligible ids pool_card_ids() drops are exactly [feed RARE, not_yet RARE], and Glass Eye's fifth screen is the Rare screen, so two Rare cards are permanently absent from it. This is the same mistake the project already fixed once elsewhere -- the batch-16 conformance finding 'reward pool = full GetUnlockedCards, not FilterForCombat (Feed/NotYet offerable)' -- and it changes both which cards appear and, because the candidate list is shorter, which index each NextItem draw lands on.

guards.what: G5 (DORMANT): C# populates ALL FIVE rewards before offering any of them; the sim populates, resolves and ADDS one screen at a time
guards.rationale: CLOSED 2026-07-28 (round 3) by the gap-queue continuation's post-section-A pass -- the turn-start split, the combat-over hook gate, Glass Eye's reward set, the out-of-combat potion action and the choose-a-card selector arm. This is a CODE change, not a re-reading of the old code. `RewardsSet.GenerateWithoutOffering` (RewardsSet.cs:125-147) populates every reward before any is offered, and Glass Eye now does the same: all five CardRewardGroups are populated, then Hook.ModifyRewards' two passes run, then the set goes to `RunState.offer_rewards`. All fifteen draws land before the first decision, so a card taken from screen 1 can no longer change what screens 2-5 drew. EXECUTED: test/test_glass_eye_reward_set.py::test_g5_every_screen_is_populated_before_any_is_offered -- the PlayerRng.Rewards counter reads 30 at every one of the five asks.  The gap it replaced read: MECHANISM: RewardsCmd.OfferCustom -> RewardsSet.Offer -> GenerateWithoutOffering loops `foreach (Reward reward in Rewards) reward.Populate()` and only then offers (RewardsSet.cs:125-147, 153-159). So all 15 cards exist before the player picks anything. glass_eye.py:63-88 loops the five rarities, populates every group, and only then calls `run.add_card` inside the loop, so screen N+1's options are created after screen N's pick has already joined the deck. DORMANT: the observable requires a listener whose card creation depends on deck contents, and the sim's card-creation path consults the pool and the rarity only -- the deck-reading hooks (after_card_added_to_deck, used by relics/book_of_five_rings.py and lucky_fysh.py) change max HP and gold rather than the pool. Porting a relic or effect whose card-reward options depend on the deck (a 'no duplicates of cards you own' filter is the obvious shape) makes it live, as does implementing G3 with a relic whose reward hook counts deck cards. Also note the interleave costs nothing in draw ORDER today, because each screen's draws are contiguous on the same stream in both orders.

guards.what: N1 (SETTLED BY EXECUTION): the reward blacklist resets per SCREEN, so the same card can be offered on two screens of the same rarity
guards.rationale: Binding rule 5: the port's comment asserts 'the reward blacklist accumulates within each rarity's screen' and that had to be checked. CardFactory.CreateForReward declares `List<CardModel> list = new List<CardModel>()` LOCALLY per call (CardFactory.cs:91) and passes it as the blacklist for each of that call's cardCount picks, so it is per-CardReward and not per-RewardsSet. RE-VERIFIED against the current shared implementation: each `CardRewardGroup.populate` (rewards.py:639-649) makes its own call to `create_reward_cards`, which builds a fresh `chosen_ids: list[str] = []` LOCALLY inside that call (rewards.py:409-412) and filters `pool` against it per pick -- so the blacklist scope is still per-screen (one `create_reward_cards` call = one of Glass Eye's five `CardRewardGroup`s), not per-RewardsSet. Executed (`py audit/tools/relic_probes_b06.py glass-eye`): the five cards granted include `breakthrough` TWICE -- once from each Common screen -- which is exactly what a per-screen blacklist permits and a per-set blacklist would forbid.

guards.what: N2: `RewardsCmd.OfferCustom` is a take-or-skip screen set; the port takes `run.select_cards('card_reward', options, 1)` and adds whatever comes back
guards.rationale: Each of the five CardRewards is individually skippable in the game. glass_eye.py:88 (run.offer_rewards) iterates whatever select_cards returns and adds it, so a policy that returns [] declines that screen -- the sim's choice seam is present and honoured. Same verdict and same reasoning as audit/records/relic/calling_bell.json G3 (the divergent thing is the sim's player-choice model, applied consistently across reward offers), binding rule 3. Recorded so a fixer does not turn the loop into an unconditional grant.

guards.what: N3: GlassEye declares NO HasUponPickupEffect, despite having a real AfterObtained
guards.rationale: GlassEye.cs has no `HasUponPickupEffect => true` override and glass_eye.py sets no has_upon_pickup_effect, so the two agree -- checked because the sibling upon-pickup relics in this batch (fragrant_mushroom, gnarled_hammer, golden_compass) all DO declare it and a missing declaration is exactly the defect batch 3 recorded for relic/byrdpip. Shadowed anyway: Relic.is_tradable (relics/base.py:132-136) already excludes ANCIENT rarity, so the flag could not change any outcome for this relic even if the source had set it.

guards.what: N4: the five rarities and their ORDER -- Common, Common, Uncommon, Uncommon, Rare -- and 3 options per screen
guards.rationale: GlassEye.cs:18-31 builds the array in that order and passes `new CardReward(options, 3, Owner)`; glass_eye.py:63 (`for name in self.SCREEN_RARITIES`) iterates the same five values in the same order, with SCREEN_RARITIES set at glass_eye.py:35 and CHOICES = 3 at glass_eye.py:33. Order is load-bearing because all five screens draw from one Rewards stream. No AscensionHelper branch in GlassEye.cs, so 3 and the rarity list are the non-ascension values.

guards.what: N5: `count = min(self.CHOICES, len(matching))` and `if count == 0: continue` (glass_eye.py:67-75) vs C#, which throws when a rarity has no candidates
guards.rationale: CardFactory.CreateForReward raises InvalidOperationException when NextItem returns null (CardFactory.cs:237-240); the sim skips the screen instead. Same reachable behaviour: the Ironclad pool has at least 3 cards at every one of the three rarities, so neither branch is taken. Recorded because the sim's tolerance would hide a pool-shrinking bug that C# would crash on.
